subject.title: fix(codex): continue after source-reply delivery instead of terminating turn

question: Should this PR become the canonical fix after it supplies exact-head live Discord/Codex proof, rather than adopting the overlapping changes from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107388?
rationale: Both branches are plausible and focused, but neither currently proves the channel-level continuation and exactly-once delivery behavior that determines whether the terminal and recovery classifications are safe together.

options.title: Require proof, then use this PR
options.body: Request a redacted live Discord/Codex run on this head and select this narrower branch if it shows progress delivery, later tool execution, final delivery, and no duplicate.

options.title: Adopt the sibling branch
options.body: Prefer the overlapping PR if maintainers want its additional model-facing `final` guidance and it first supplies equivalent live proof.

options.title: Replace both branches
options.body: Close both candidates and implement a maintainer-owned consolidation if the terminal and recovery semantics need broader restructuring.

recommendation.title: Require proof, then use this PR
recommendation.body: Request a redacted live Discord/Codex run on this head and select this narrower branch if it shows progress delivery, later tool execution, final delivery, and no duplicate.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced and merged the current Codex source-reply completion semantics, making them the strongest history-based owner for confirming the intended termination and recovery contract.
